# Generated files

What `cech build` writes in a marketplace, and from what ([ADR 18](../adr/0018-generated-files.md)).
Change the source and run the build again; never edit a generated file by hand.

## Hand-written sources

Per plugin, two files hold hand-written metadata, and the build fills in the rest:

- `SKILL.md`: the `name`, the `description`, any `metadata`, and the skill itself;
- `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`: every other field, such as `name`, `author`, `license` and `dependencies`, but not `description`, `version` or, in an extension, the `marketplace` of a dependency on a CECH plugin.

The marketplace's own data is in `data/marketplace.toml` ([A marketplace](marketplace.md#the-data-file)).

## Each `plugin.json`

- `description` is copied from `SKILL.md`.
- `version` is `0.0.0-dev`, or `V` in a release build ([A marketplace](marketplace.md#release-builds)).
- A field the build adds goes right after `name`.
- In an extension, each dependency written as an object whose `name` starts with `cech-` gets a `marketplace`: the name of the CECH release in the `cech` key, such as `cech-0-1-0` for `0.1.0`.
- Every other byte of the file stays as it was.

## The catalogue

`.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` has:

- a `name`: the namespace, or `<namespace>-V` in a release build;
- the `description` and `owner` from `data/marketplace.toml`;
- for each plugin, its `name`, `source`, `description` and `category`, the category taken from its folder, sorted by category and then by name.

## Codex agents

Beside each reviewer agent's Markdown in a plugin's `agents/`, the build writes a Codex agent, `agents/<agent>.toml`.
Its first line names the Markdown it came from; then come `name`, `description`, `sandbox_mode = "read-only"`, and `developer_instructions`, which holds the Markdown's text after the frontmatter.
The build removes any other `.toml` file in `agents/`.

## Licence copies

Each skill folder gets `skills/<name>/LICENSE`, an exact copy of the root `LICENSE`, so a skill copied without its plugin keeps its licence.
Without a root `LICENSE`, the build writes no copy, and leaves alone any copy already there.

## The code owners file

When `data/marketplace.toml` has a `team`, the build writes `.github/CODEOWNERS`:

1. first, a catch-all line, `* <team>`;
2. then, for each plugin, a line for `/<plugin folder>/` that names its owner and its maintainers.

- The owner is `<user>` when the manifest's `author.url` is `https://github.com/<user>`, unless `<user>` is the team's organisation.
- The maintainers are the GitHub user names in the manifest's `metadata.maintainers`.
- Each name appears once, whatever its case.
- The build takes the names from the manifests alone, without network access.
- A plugin with no one to name gets no line, and is left to the catch-all team.
- Without a `team`, the build writes no code owners file, and removes one that starts with `# Generated by cech build`, leaving any other.

## The catalogue page

`docs/catalogue.md` has a table of the categories and what each holds, CECH's first and then any the extension adds, and a table per category of its plugins and their descriptions.

## Every generated file

- A file whose format allows comments starts with a line saying that `cech build` generated it; a licence copy has none.
- A file the build writes from scratch has LF line ends and a final newline; a file it rewrites keeps its mode.
- The output is the same on every OS, and a second build changes nothing.
- `cech build --check` writes nothing and fails when any generated file differs from what the build would write; it is the `build:check` gate.
